Dark Prince Road #3

My Dark Prince

Parker S. Huntington, L.J. Shen

3.94
20,644 ratings2,503 reviews
Rate this book
This Sleeping Beauty woke up...
In a nightmare.

From Wall Street Journal bestsellers L.J. Shen and Parker S. Huntington comes a twisted second-chance romance between a prince haunted by a dark secret and his reluctant Sleeping Beauty.

Oliver
I don’t usually trap women with amnesia into marriage.
But I guess there’s a first time for everything.
When the woman of my dreams falls into my lap, I can’t help but wonder what else she can do in that position.
She’s here. In my house. At my mercy.
And she thinks we’ve been lovers the entire decade we spent apart.
Briar and I have always been unfinished business.
Now it’s time to seal the deal.

Briar
I’m marrying a beautiful monster.
A crooked fraud. America’s wealthiest bachelor.
He claims we’re in love, yet all I taste in our kisses is hate and lust.
I don’t remember why or how.
But I do remember he’s the enemy.
Now, I’m stuck inside a nightmare.
And Oliver will do anything to keep me in the dark.

Authors’ Note: My Dark Prince is a standalone enemies-to-lovers Sleeping Beauty retelling, in which a damaged billionaire with a dark past and his childhood sweetheart fall in love—literally. It is set in the decadent Dark Prince Road universe.

I truly enjoyed the first 50% of the book, BUT the second half ruined it for me. This book had a strong start and I could see myself rating this 4 stars but then the second half happened. It dragged on and on to the extent, I had to force myself to finish it.

The limited content in there did not justify its huge length— 533 pages. This book has 99 chapters for god's sake. Add the epilogue and it's 100. Also, the miscommunication trope truly got on my nerves. Had they communicated like mature adults, 300 pages could've easily been cut short.

I liked the main leads in the start but they got really annoying as I went further into the book. They're in their early thirties so why are they behaving like teenagers? I personally felt there was no maturity or emotional intelligence on their part.

Honestly the side characters were even more immature and intolerable in this book (I haven't read the first two books) but after seeing their cameos over here, I'm glad I didn't. The only character I truly adored was Sebastian (mmc’s brother) I really hope the author writes his book and does justice to his amazing personality.

Also what's up with the group chat? There are literally 20 chapters dedicated to the group chat among the characters and that's INSANE. Like WHY?? This book is already unnecessarily long, we didn't need 20 chapters dedicated for the group texts alone. If it were 3-4 chapters I could've gotten behind but wtf were the co-authors thinking while writing this?

All I can say is that, in my opinion, this book had SO much potential that is now completely wasted.

Okay, so looking at my rating… Pre-release me is judging so hard right now. And let me just say—the amnesia trope? Usually, I hate it. 😩 But THIS?! THIS is the only time I’ve actually loved it. 😍 It just worked. Also, I low-key think Briar replacing Frankie was a last-minute author decision because EXPLAIN THAT SCENE FROM BOOK 2. 🫠

TL;DR—this book owned me. Go read it. Immediately. 🔥

────୨ৎ────────୨ৎ────────୨ৎ────

Let me just say this first: WHO TF IS BRIAR?! This was supposed to be Frankie and Oliver's story! Like, the betrayal here is REAL. 😭 We spent two books thinking these two were endgame—AND THEN THIS?! What is the meaning of doing us dirty like this? I’m screaming.

Remember this scene from Book 2?! 👇
Frankie and Oliver busting in, looking messy and sus, lipstick smudges everywhere, and everyone in the room side-eyeing the hell out of them like “WE KNOW WHAT YOU DID.” And then the authors drop this bomb on us in Book 3?! You’re telling me after all that... they won’t be together? I need answers. Like, yesterday.

Also, can we talk about this amnesia trope nonsense? My literal most hated trope ever. Missed communication? Fine. Accidental pregnancy? I'll live. But amnesia? It’s giving rage. And now the theory is that Frankie lost her memory and became Briar? That makes zero sense because HELLO, Dallas (Frankie’s sister) is RIGHT THERE. So… either I’m delusional, or I’m rating this 1 star out of pure spite.

And Oliver? Babe, why are you acting like Briar has been the love of your life for decades? You spent two books as a certified manwhore, and now this?!

Okay, okay, deep breaths. Maybe Frankie’s story is coming later. Maybe Briar is low-key amazing, and I’ll love her. But for now, I’m manifesting some serious damage control. Delulu is truly the solulu. 😇

Final Thoughts:
1. Still bitter.
2. Still confused.
3. Still gonna read because I’m trash for this series. 😭

Release day cannot come soon enough.

March 10, 2024
Welp, I ate my words. Isn't that just amazing?! 🥲 Curiosity about the reviews suggesting that Oliver isn't exactly the character he seemed to be in prior books (a nasty walking STD) and that male cover really got the better of me. 🫠🫣

The first 60% was okay-ish, I think??? I mean, the amnesia thing made sense, as did how the MCs interacted with one another.

But when Briar (33) regained her memories and still decided to go back to Ollie's house since Seb had asked her, I just lost all interest. Probably because I hoped she'd show indifference, pettiness, or cling to her anger (I'm petty 🤷‍♀️), but nope, her hormones just took over. 🥴 She's angry, or so she claims, but she still lets him touch her and do things to her body. And Ollie was more than happy to oblige because he finally had the only woman he ever loved. Although she claimed that staying there was for Seb's sake and the rational thing to do given that it's only for three months, readers know deep down that isn't the case at all. Whether she admits it or not, she remains in love with him despite the years and the pain he has caused her.

Tbf, Oliver (34) was dealing with his own stuff as well. They were young and didn’t really know better, and when he got that ultimatum to pick between his brother or Briar, he chose the former without hesitation, though it came with a lot of regret and heartbreak. After that, he started to think that all he did was bring pain to the people around him, and that maybe he didn't deserve any good things in life or love, for that matter. Hence, the start of his "act/pretending" to be the notorious dumbass manwh*re.

Apparently, he's not a hoe (shocker). It turns out he only had sex twice in his life. He said he was only pretending to be an airhead playboy and not to believe anything the gossip magazines and websites say about him. He said that after he and Briar broke up, he had just one ONS, but it sucked, and he gave up after. So, after knowing that info, I think readers are supposed to believe that he had been celibate FOR YEARS.

Oh, and he's also not dumb and jobless. It turns out he has been secretly running his family's business for more than a decade, despite the fact that his father is still in charge. He's also not careless, like the way he carries himself, and one of his weaknesses is that he cares too deeply and too much.

It would seem that he just carefully constructed that image and has been maintaining it for so long so that people won't try to dig deep about him. 🤔

Does this 180-degree turn of events make sense? Nope, not one bit. Do I believe any of it? Nuh-uh.

Somehow it still seems like there are so many contradictions between what he thinks/says (inner monologues), how he was portrayed in the previous books, and what he claims is his reality. 🤧

I think the authors tried their best to redeem Ollie's character by making him as this secretly sensible and responsible man. Showing that there's more to him than his facade and the misunderstandings surrounding him. But, idk, it felt unconvincing and just really doesn't make any sense to ME.

For some reason, I really believe that their initial concept for him was to be this manwh*re from the start, but then they changed their minds and completely flipped his personality and reputation around. 🤷‍♀️🤔

As for Briar, she was just so...meh. Idk, she just didn't intrigue me at all. Aside from being an intimacy coordinator, there’s just not much that stands out about her. I mean, I felt sad for her when she was young; it's not her fault her parents were nasty people. But the way I see it, that was all she had to give, along with her love for Ollie and his brother, Seb. I just didn't like her character; in fact, I had more fun reading about Dallas and her shenanigans, and she's only a side character in this story.

A lot went down in the last quarter, and it feels like everything was crammed in there. Did it improve the story? Imo, marginally. Things started to look up and eventually made more sense. Still, I don't think this book needs to be over 400 pages. Some of the scenes/chapters appear to be fillers that add nothing to the overall experience.

This story was chaotic, and I'm not really sure if that's a good thing or a bad thing. Some parts were fun, while others didn't quite hit the mark for me, and tbh, I'm still not sure how I feel overall about Ollie and Briar's story. Anyway, it all boils down to personal preference, and to each their own as always.


Book info:
- Second chance (15 yrs)
- Childhood friends/lovers to enemies
- Fake engagement
- Post traumatic amnesia
- Parental abandonment
- Facial disfigurement (side char, by an accident)
- Dual V (in the past)
- Slowburn
- No cheating, OM/OW
- Separation (1 month, LDR)
- HEA (married)
- Bonus epilogue (thru newsletter, 1 yr, planning to have a baby)


Notes:
- Separation (when they were 18/19). He claimed he had one hookup after ghosting (breaking up with) her. It was never said how long they had "broken up" before he did it. Apparently, that was his second (and final) sexual encounter. 🤷‍♀️ Meanwhile, Briar's had her share of boyfriends, and based on what happens in this book, readers can assume that she's probably had more action in the last 15 years than Ollie has.
- I'm really unsure about how to feel about Seb; I'm kind of torn when it comes to his character. Imo, I think he was a jealous and selfish person, and he brought a lot of his own misery on himself. But I'm still intrigued about his story, if he ever gets one.

Oliver von Bismarck. Duke of Carinthia. Unofficial CEO of The Grand Regent. In short, our own Ollie. This man made me realize how single i am. He made me smile, giggle, blush, giddy, sad, laugh, scream, cry, heartbroken and every single emotion i expect from a book boyfriend. “That I’m yours. Completely. Unconditionally. Tragically. I will take your hate over anyone else’s love. Your anger over anyone else’s compassion. Your tears over anyone else’s smiles. A moment with you over anyone else’s forever. You’re the one.”

Before this book, adjectives i had used for Ollie:
Man-whore with weird sexual innuendoes, Gross, Dumb, Crass, Immature, Unserious.

After finishing his book:
Loverboy, Romantic, Caring, Protective, Passionate, Selfless, Swoony, Simp, Charismatic, A perfect husband material.🤌

The phases of their journey in a nutshell:

“Ollie, It feels like the sky is falling.”
“If the sky falls, I’ll hold it up for you.”

This time if the sky falls, I’ll hold it up for you.”

Lastly, what made this book more special was this “Dark Prince Road” found family. The dynamics between Ollie, Zach and Romeo, and even Dallas and Farrow, their bickering and interactions, how they are always for each other with their unhingedly-chaotic personalities and antics, and most importantly the group chats, I adore everything about this family. Petition to the authors to publish a whole long ass book of their GCs and i will devour it with a popcorn bowl istfg😌

“You’re not the shadow. I am. You are the living, breathing organism inside of me. I’m just here for the ride.”

This book is not just a love-story, it is more than that. It show us loneliness, self-loathing, guilt, hurt, sacrifices, trauma, forgiveness, redemption, acceptance, healing and finally finding a family while embracing happiness, portrayed in a light-hearted way. The underline motives of this book made a deep remarkable imprint on my soul.

When Love Refuses to Stay Buried



The following ratings are out of 5:
Romance: ❤️💚💙💛🩷
Chemistry: 🧪🧪🧪🧪🧪
Spice: 🌶️🌶️🌶️🌶️🌶️
Story/Plot: 📕📗📘📙📔
World building: 🌏🌍🌎🌍🌏
Character development: 🤓😟🤯😎🥰
Narration: 🎙🎙🎙🎙🎙
Narration Type: Duet Narration

My Dark Prince by L.J. Shen and Parker S. Huntington is a dark and emotionally layered retelling of Sleeping Beauty, trading in magic and innocence for guilt, secrets, and a love story shaped by years of separation and unresolved pain.

Characters & Backgrounds

Oliver Von Bismarck, the hidden force behind The Grand Regent hotel empire, is a man living behind a carefully crafted mask. To the public, he is a reckless playboy, a lush, and a tabloid favorite who thrives on scandal. Beneath that persona, however, lies a deeply burdened individual carrying guilt from a past mistake that continues to haunt him. His avoidance of Briar for fifteen years speaks to the weight of that secret, and his self-destructive reputation feels less like indulgence and more like punishment.

Briar “Rose” Auer is a strong and quietly resilient heroine whose life has been shaped by rejection and betrayal. Raised by parents who never truly loved her, she eventually learns the devastating truth about her biological father and the reasons behind her upbringing. Rather than breaking her, these experiences sharpen her independence. As an adult, she has built a career as an intimacy coordinator, a role that subtly reflects her need for control and boundaries in a world that once denied her both.

Together, Oliver and Briar share a past filled with innocence that was abruptly shattered, leaving behind unresolved emotions and lingering wounds that neither has been able to escape.

Plot Summary

The story moves between past and present, showing the deep bond Oliver and Briar once shared during childhood summers and the moment everything changed. The revelation about Briar’s parentage and the events surrounding it create a fracture inside Briar and though she still sees Ollie for the next few summers, but is afraid that he won’t continue to love her like he used to since even her own parents can’t find it within themselves to love he.r

Fifteen years later, fate forces them back into each other’s orbit when Briar is working on a film being shot at one of the Grand Regent hotels. Their reunion is anything but smooth. Oliver is desperate to confront the past, while Briar refuses to reopen old wounds. The tension between them is immediate and charged, built on years of unanswered questions and emotional scars.

A turning point comes when Briar is injured and falls into a pond, forcing Oliver into action. His frantic attempt to save her strips away his carefully maintained façade and reveals the depth of his feelings and guilt. From there, the story unfolds as a slow unraveling of secrets, pushing both characters to confront what happened all those years ago and whether redemption and forgiveness are possible.

Highlights & Low Points

One of the strongest aspects of My Dark Prince is its emotional intensity. The authors excel at building a palpable sense of longing and tension between Oliver and Briar. Their shared history adds weight to every interaction, making even small moments feel significant. When Briar awakens in the hospital she can’t remember the last fifteen years, but the last thing she remembers was Oliver telling her he loved her when she was sixteen and the fact that he is in her life currently, she assumes that they have been together all along.

Oliver’s character stands out for his complexity. His public persona contrasted with his private reality creates a compelling internal conflict, and his guilt-driven behavior adds depth to his actions. Briar, meanwhile, is a grounded and capable heroine whose strength lies in her restraint and self-respect. Oliver’s neighbors and best friends were awesome and one of the best parts of this book.

The atmosphere is another highlight. The luxurious hotel and mansion settings contrast beautifully with the darker emotional undertones, reinforcing the idea that appearances can be deceiving. I also usually hate books where either of the main characters is a virgin, but in this case, I loved the flashback scene to the first time they made love, when they were both virgins. It was surprisingly sweet and genuine, and I loved how they joked afterwards.

On the downside, the pacing can feel uneven at times, particularly in the middle where the push and pull between the characters occasionally drags. Some readers may also find Oliver’s secrecy frustrating, especially when it prolongs misunderstandings that could have been addressed sooner. Additionally, the heavy emotional themes and morally gray behavior may not appeal to those looking for a lighter or more traditional romance.

Narration (Christian Fox & Andi Arndt)

The audiobook narration by Christian Fox and Andi Arndt adds another layer of depth to the story.

Christian Fox delivers Oliver’s character with a compelling mix of arrogance and vulnerability. His performance captures both the polished public image and the underlying torment, making Oliver’s internal struggle feel authentic and engaging.

Andi Arndt brings Briar to life with emotional nuance and strength. She balances Briar’s vulnerability with her resilience, ensuring that the character never feels weak despite everything she has endured.

Together, their performances enhance the chemistry between the characters and elevate the emotional stakes of the story.

Final Thoughts

My Dark Prince is a haunting and emotionally driven retelling of Sleeping Beauty that leans heavily into themes of guilt, identity, and second chances. It replaces the traditional notion of a cursed sleep with emotional paralysis, where both characters are stuck in the past until they confront it.

While it may not be for every reader due to its darker tone and complex characters, fans of angsty, character-driven romance will find it deeply compelling. This is a story about facing the truth, no matter how painful, and discovering whether love can survive the weight of long-buried secrets.
